audit.whatIsWrong: The entry systematically swaps K'Sante's Q and W. content spikes[0].text says "Q3 (Path Maker) knock-up plus W pull"; content mid says "Q3 Path Maker knocks you up and his W (grab) pins you"; whys[2] says "Q3 knock-up at 3"; wants.foe[0] says "Land Q3 knock-up".
audit.why: Path Maker is his W, not his Q. The knock-back and stun are W. The pull is Q (Ntofo Strikes) and it fires at 2 stacks, not 3. So every one of these lines tells the player to watch the wrong ability for the wrong effect at the wrong stack count. A Zac dodging "Q3 knock-up" is dodging something that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Q = Ntofo Strikes, 450 range, 3.5s, pulls in at 2 stacks. W = Path Maker, knocks back and stuns. Applied across whys[2], spikes[0].text, wants.foe[0], mid and the dosFull/dontsFull triggers.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (Q "At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in"; W "Path Maker ... dashes, knocking back and stunning enemies")

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text and whys[4] treat All Out as pure upside for K'Sante ("shreds your armour", "owning the fight"), and the advice is "do not E in when he has R up".
audit.why: All Out is explicitly a trade-off: he gains damage and healing "at the cost of reduced defenses". It is the window in which he is least tanky. Two further things change that nothing in the entry mentions: while All Out, Path Maker no longer knocks back or stuns, so his hard-CC punish on your engage disappears, and his only remaining lock is the Q 2-stack pull. The correct read is the opposite of the one on the page - you want the fight after he commits All Out, not before.
audit.corrected: Reframed in whys[4], spikes[1].text, mid and late.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (R "at the cost of reduced defenses"; W "When All Out ... no longer knocks back or stuns")

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] and early call K'Sante's Q the ranged tool that out-pokes Zac's "melee Q", and both attribute true damage to his passive.
audit.why: Ntofo Strikes is 450 range; Zac's Stretching Strikes is 800. Zac has nearly double the reach, so the range framing is backwards. And Dauntless Instinct does not deal true damage - it marks a target to take more damage from his next attack. The true-damage flag in his kit sits on W, not the passive.
audit.corrected: whys[0] and early now give the real ranges (450 vs 800) and describe Dauntless Instinct as a damage mark.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (Q range 450, P "mark targets to take more damage on his next Attack")

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text says his first-item trade patterns "beat your W (Unstable Matter) percent-damage exchange", and whys[3] says his trades "out-value your W".
audit.why: Backwards. Unstable Matter deals a percentage of the target's MAXIMUM health, so it scales with how much health the enemy stacks. K'Sante is the highest-health-stacking opponent in this matchup pool - he is the single best target for W that Zac faces, not a counter to it. Telling a Zac his W loses to a health-stacking tank inverts his itemisation read.
audit.corrected: whys[3] and spikes[2].text now say W is at its best here precisely because he stacks health.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (W "a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage")

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives K'Sante all 7 of 7 stages while Zac wins the matchup 54.77% over 199 games.
audit.why: A clean sweep for the side that loses the matchup is the largest chart/data contradiction in this slice, and 199 games is a solid sample. K'Sante does own the laning phase, so the fix is not to flip it wholesale - it is to stop the sweep at the point where Zac's scaling and engage actually take over.
audit.corrected: K'Sante / K'Sante / K'Sante / K'Sante / Skill / Skill / Zac.

audit.whatIsWrong: No note that Path Maker reduces the damage he takes while charging.
audit.why: W is a charge-then-dash. During the charge he takes reduced damage, so damage poured into the wind-up is partly wasted. That is a concrete "do not press this now" window, and it is the reason short trades into a charging K'Sante feel worse than they look.
audit.corrected: Noted alongside the W correction in spikes[0].text.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (W "K'Sante charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes")

audit.why: Nothing in the on-disk text makes a patch-specific claim that 26.15 contradicts, and I have no verified 26.15 change for either champion to cite. Left alone rather than guessed at.

edits.before: K'Sante's ranged Q and passive true damage out-poke your melee Q at level 1.
edits.after: K'Sante's Q is 450 range to your 800, but his passive mark hits harder.

edits.before: Q3 knock-up at 3 pins you and denies your E escape.
edits.after: At 3 his Q pulls you in at 2 stacks, on a 3.5s cooldown.

edits.before: Through 4-5 his sustained trades and armour shred out-value your W.
edits.after: Through 4-5 he out-trades you, though your W punishes his HP most.

edits.before: All-Out at 6 shreds your armour and wall-slams you, owning the fight.
edits.after: All Out at 6 wall-slams you, but it strips his own resistances too.

edits.before: His first item sustain keeps him ahead of your blob health.
edits.after: First item is even: his sustain against your blob health.

edits.before: Late, his repositioning undoes your engages, so the matchup stays his.
edits.after: Late, your engage range and HP pool beat a low-resist All Out form.

edits.before: K'Sante's Q3 (Path Maker) knock-up plus W pull disrupts your E landing, and his passive true-damage stacks chunk you every trade even through your blob health.
edits.after: K'Sante's Q pulls you in at 2 stacks and his W (Path Maker) knocks back and stuns, wrecking your E landing — and W takes reduced damage all through its charge-up.

edits.before: All Out flips the fight: he shreds your armour, gains range, and can wall-slam you back into tower — do not E in when he has R up.
edits.after: All Out flips the fight — he wall-slams you through terrain and his damage jumps. But it also cuts his resistances and his W stops stunning.

edits.before: After his first item (Sundered Sky or Hollow Radiance) his sustained trade patterns beat your W (Unstable Matter) percent-damage exchange.
edits.after: After his first item his sustained trades bite, but W (Unstable Matter) burns percent max health — the health he stacks to tank you is what feeds it.

edits.before: Land Q3 knock-up to lock you before you can E out
edits.after: Land the W stun to lock you before you can E out

edits.before: K'Sante out-trades you at 1-2 — his Q pokes with range and his passive tacks on true damage every hit while your only tool is a clunky Q (Stretching Strikes) that he sidesteps. Don't try to win short trades; last-hit safe and use your passive blobs to eat harass.
edits.after: K'Sante out-trades you at 1-2, but not on range — Ntofo Strikes is 450 to your Q's 800. It costs 20 mana on a 3.5s cooldown, so he throws it constantly, and Dauntless Instinct marks you so his next auto lands harder. Last-hit safe and eat the harass with blobs.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are his strongest window: Q3 Path Maker knocks you up and his W (grab) pins you so your E (Elastic Slingshot) engage gets punished, and at 6 All-Out shreds your armour and gives him the range to chase you down. Ping for a gank rather than forcing it yourself.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 are his strongest window: W (Path Maker) knocks back and stuns while Q pulls you in at 2 stacks, so your E (Elastic Slingshot) engage keeps getting punished. At 6 All Out buys him damage and chase range — but it also strips his resistances and his W stops stunning. Ping for a gank.

edits.before: With items K'Sante's dueling and repositioning only grow — his All-Out dash undoes your R knock-up in fights. Play him as a peel/disengage problem, group with your team, and use E-flash engages on his backline instead of trading into him.
edits.after: With items K'Sante duels and repositions better, yet All Out is exactly when his resistances are lowest and his W can no longer stun you out of an engage. Group, use E-flash onto his backline, and take the fight after he has committed R rather than before it.

notes: K'Sante is the worst entry in this slice: a 7/7 level chart for the side that loses 54.77% of 199 games, plus a systematic Q/W ability swap repeated in four places. The packet's only flagged suspectName here was "Let's Bounce", which is a false positive - the on-disk text already reads "R (Let's Bounce!)" and the detector strips the exclamation mark. The real name errors (Path Maker attributed to Q, "Q3" for a 2-stack effect) were not flagged at all. The three win[] edits are short label fields and will fail a literal +/-10% length band.
